news.title: Chelsea vs Luton: Key statistics and facts
news.body_en: Chelsea begin our Carabao Cup campaign at the second-round stage, with a tie against League One Luton Town. Here are all the facts and figures you need ahead of the Hatters' visit to Stamford Bridge. Chelsea meet Luton Town for the first time since December 2023. Chelsea and Luton have never met in the League Cup before. We have faced them five times in the FA Cup, winning four, while our only Full Members’ Cup meeting ended in defeat on penalties. 	The Blues have won our past five meetings with Luton, starting with the 1994 FA Cup semi-final at Wembley. We then beat the Hatters in the FA Cup in both 2021 and 2022, before completing a Premier League double over them in 2023/24.	Luton’s last win at Stamford Bridge was 3-1 in September 1986 in the old First Division. Kerry Dixon scored our goal in front of just over 13,000 fans. Joao Pedro’s opener against Fulham, timed at 31 seconds, was our quickest goal since October 2016, when Pedro scored against Manchester United at Stamford Bridge after 30 seconds. The Blues went on to win 4-0 on that occasion. This will be Chelsea’s third appearance in the League Cup second round in the past 30 years. The previous two both came at Stamford Bridge - a 3-2 win over Bristol Rovers in 2016 and a 2-1 victory against Wimbledon in 2023. Chelsea have advanced from 27 of our last 28 League Cup ties against teams from outside the top flight, including each of the last 19, since losing on penalties to Burnley in November 2008. Chelsea last went out in the League Cup second round in 1995/96, losing to Stoke City over two legs. After a goalless draw at the Victoria Ground, we were beaten 1-0 at Stamford Bridge. The last time Chelsea were eliminated from the competition by a lower-division side was in the fourth round in November 2008, when we lost 5-4 on penalties to Burnley after a 1-1 draw. Thursday’s game will be Chelsea’s 107th League Cup match at Stamford Bridge, having won 69 per cent of the previous 106 (five after a penalty shootout). Chelsea lost our most recent Carabao Cup home match, against Arsenal in last season’s semi-final first leg. Our previous defeat at Stamford Bridge in the competition came against Manchester United in 2019. If the aggregate scores are level after 90 minutes, the tie will be decided on penalties as there is no extra time in this competition until the semi-final stage. It has been nearly three years since our last penalty shootout, when we beat Newcastle United 4-2 in the League Cup quarter-final in December 2023. Last Saturday they drew 2-2 with Notts County at Kenilworth Road. They are third in League One after two rounds of games. The Hatters beat League Two side Gillingham 3-0 away in the Carabao Cup first round. Their scorers were Nahki Wells, Benny Benagr and Gideon Kodua. Luton ended last season with three straight wins and have won two and drawn one this term, extending their unbeaten run to 15 matches since their last defeat on 7 March. After their 2023/24 Premier League campaign, Luton suffered back-to-back relegations into League One, before missing out on the play-offs last season by just one point. The most recent occasion Luton were involved in a shootout was in December last year, when they lost 4-2 on penalties to Fleetwood in the FA Cup second round. Luton have been eliminated from eight of their past nine ties against Premier League opponents in the League Cup. The Hatters have progressed from three of their last four Carabao Cup second-round ties, but lost on penalties to Queens Park Rangers in their most recent appearance at this stage, in 2024/25. Former Blues academy players Kasey Palmer and George Saville play for Luton. Jack Wilshere has never managed a side against Chelsea. As a player against the Blues, he won three games with two draws and seven defeats between 2010 and 2020, with Bolton Wanderers, Arsenal, Bournemouth and West Ham United. Since being appointed manager last October, Wilshere has recorded a 52 per cent win rate and led Luton to EFL Trophy victory at Wembley in April. news.title: Axel Disasi completes Crystal Palace loan switch
news.body_en: Chelsea defender Axel Disasi has joined Crystal Palace on loan for the 2026/27 season. The centre-back moved to Stamford Bridge from AS Monaco in August 2023 and has made more than 60 appearances in blue. The France international started our first eight matches in the victorious UEFA Conference League campaign in 2024/25, before finishing the season on loan at Aston Villa. Disasi then spent the second half of last season on loan at West Ham, starting 16 of their 17 matches in all competitions. Everyone at Chelsea wishes Axel well and looks forward to following his progress during his time with Crystal Palace.

news.title: Chelsea’s fastest Premier League goals
news.body_en: Joao Pedro gave Chelsea an early lead inside the first minute at Fulham, adding his name to the list of the Blues’ fastest scorers in the Premier League. The Brazilian opened the scoring with just 31 seconds on the clock at Craven Cottage on Monday night, breaking clear from Cole Palmer’s flick to make a flying start to the 2026/27 campaign and set us on our way to a 3-2 victory. It was officially the earliest goal ever on the Premier League’s opening weekend, but only good enough to come sixth on the all-time list of Chelsea’s fastest goalscorers in that competition. Here are the five players who found the net quicker for the Blues in the Premier League… Chelsea blew Man Utd away on Jose Mourinho’s return to Stamford Bridge with the Red Devils. It was Pedro who got the ball rolling on the thrashing when the visiting defenders dawdled in a moment of miscommunication. There was no such hesitancy from our Spanish forward, who took full advantage to round the keeper and slot in. It wasn’t to be Chelsea’s day, as Arsenal came back to take the win at Stamford Bridge and go seven points clear at the top of the Premier League table, but we had got off to the best possible start. That came when Gudjohnsen showed his instincts in the box to control Geremi’s cross brilliantly and fire the opening goal past the keeper. Manchester United’s run of 29 games without defeat came to an emphatic end at Stamford Bridge, as Chelsea turned on the style. The Blues went on the attack right from kick-off, giving Dan Petrescu the chance to cross. When United goalkeeper Massimo Taibi came to collect but collided with one of his defenders, Poyet gratefully headed into the empty net. The Blues were heavy favourites against newly-promoted Nottingham Forest when we met at the Bridge early in the 1998/99 campaign, despite the visitors' decent start to the season. We underlined that status early on, though, with a goal all of Zola’s own making. It was his cross into the box from a throw-in on the left which created the chance. When Forest failed to clear their lines, the Italian was there following in on his own cross to place a first-time finish into the bottom corner. Chelsea had lost two home games in a row when Leicester came to Stamford Bridge looking to be the next visiting side to inflict pain on the Blues. This time we raced into an early, and unassailable, lead. An early foul gifted us a free-kick on the halfway line and Dennis Wise took the chance to run clear into space. He then picked out a teasing angled cross to the back post, where Spencer floated in the air to meet it and head down into the net.

Chelsea and FPT extend strategic partnership into 2026/27 season
news.body_en: Chelsea Football Club and Global Technology Services provider FPT Corporation today announce the extension of our existing partnership for the 2026/27 season. Since first joining forces in 2025, Chelsea and FPT have worked closely together to transform the club’s digital capabilities and enhance the club’s fan engagement to bring Chelsea fans across the world closer to club. With FPT’s market-leading technology solutions and expertise, together Chelsea and FPT have delivered on a number of key projects. Megastore Express – a new mobile-first click-and-collect system – was unveiled in January and streamlines the retail experience for fans on matchdays. A new Official Supporters Club platform was also launched earlier this year and has become the new home for fans from across the world to build supporter groups, join in club activities and be a part of the Chelsea community. These transformative initiatives are a marker of our shared vision to enhance how the club engages with our ever-growing global fan base, enriching the fan experience at Stamford Bridge and beyond. The extension of this partnership is a celebration of the significant progress FPT and Chelsea have made together and marks a renewed commitment to continue the club’s digital transformation journey. Oli Boden, partnership sales director at Chelsea FC, said: 'At Chelsea we are continually focused on innovating and unlocking the opportunities technology and AI-based solutions present to grow our digital presence and bring our fans closer to the club. ‘Together we have delivered significant projects that have transformed the way in which fans can engage with the club. As we embark on the next stage of our partnership with FPT, we reaffirm our commitment to accelerating innovation and enriching the fan experience for our supporters at home and abroad.’‘This partnership reaffirms the qualities that Chelsea FC saw in FPT from the beginning: the ability to deliver at speed and scale, a co-creation mindset, and an AI-driven approach to innovation,’ said Mark Scrivens, CEO of FPT in the United Kingdom. ‘Our teams will continue working side by side to turn ambitious concepts into live, fan-focused solutions, which is a testament to the talent, agility, and engineering excellence of our people, and demonstrates how FPT helps organisations accelerate transformation while remaining focused on delivering measurable outcomes.’

news.title: PGA South League report: London City Under-21s 0-8 Chelsea Women’s Under-18s
news.body_en: Chelsea Women’s Under-18s began their Professional Game Academy South League campaign in impressive fashion, securing an 8-0 victory away at London City Lionesses Under-21s on Wednesday evening. Chelsea Women's Under-18s, who play in the PGA Under-21 Women's League, were ahead inside seven minutes on Wednesday through Stevie Sinclair and established a two-goal advantage before the interval thanks to Maisie Brickell's strike. After the break, Chelsea added six more goals, with Chelsea N'Drin, Sinclair and Brickell all ending the match with two goals, while Jahyma Putman and Tess Finn also added their names to the scoresheet. Chelsea dominated possession throughout and combined attacking quality with defensive discipline to ensure they opened the new league season with both three points and a clean sheet. Chelsea made a positive start and moved in front after seven minutes. Victoria Rudz's clipped pass into the wide channel allowed Brickell to advance down the flank and deliver a cross into the box. Sinclair arrived from midfield and fired home from the edge of the area to give the Blues an early lead. The second goal arrived after 17 minutes and again involved Rudz and Brickell. Spotting space beyond the London City back line, Rudz played forward into the right channel, where Brickell drove towards goal before cutting across her defender and finishing at the near post. Chelsea continued to control possession and territory for the remainder of the first half, limiting opportunities for the hosts while taking a deserved two-goal advantage into the interval. A triple substitution at the break helped maintain Chelsea's momentum and a third goal arrived six minutes into the second half. After Putman switched play to Zoe Ciccardini, the defender found Sinclair's run in behind. The goalkeeper showed bravery to deny Sinclair's initial effort, but N'Drin reacted quickest to convert the rebound. Chelsea continued to press aggressively and nearly extended the lead further when N'Drin was brought down in the penalty area after a high regain. Sinclair's resulting penalty was saved, but the Blues were adding to the scoresheet once again soon after. The fourth goal arrived on 76 minutes when combinations around the edge of the box by Finn and N’Drin helped create space for Sinclair, who took a touch beyond the last defender before finishing confidently. A minute later Chelsea struck again. Finn recovered possession high up the pitch and switched play to Putman, who advanced towards goal before spinning past the goalkeeper and calmly finishing into an empty net. Finn then added her own name to the scoresheet on 86 minutes. After some quick combinations the ball was worked wide to Putman at left wing, she showed positive 1v1 play to get to the byline to pull the ball back to the edge of the box for the arriving Finn, who’s placed shot to the goalkeeper’s right added another. Three minutes later, N’Drin and Gregory helped win possession high up the pitch and the latter played into Brickell on the edge of the box. She turned and placed a composed finish across goal for Chelsea's seventh. There was still time for one more. Deep into added time, Sinclair dropped low to combine with Ciccardini, who was able to find Storey inside the pitch, with good vision and quick play. Storey played forward through the defensive line of London City Lionesses to find Brickell in the wide area. After some more positive play, Brickell delivered a lofted cross into the box which was met by N’Drin in the air to score the final goal. The result means Chelsea Women Under-18s sit top of the Professional Game Academy South League table thanks to their eight-goal winning margin. Chelsea's next fixture sees us travel to face Wycombe Wanderers Women in the senior Women's National League Cup on Thursday. The Blues then return to Professional Game Academy South League action on Sunday 30 August when Crystal Palace visit. news.title: EFL Trophy: Bristol Rovers 2-2 Cobham Next Gen (2-4 on pens)
news.body_en: Cobham Next Gen showed real heart as we came from two goals down to beat Bristol Rovers on penalties in our opening EFL Trophy fixture. The hosts led at the interval through Mees Rijks and extended their advantage via Joe Quigley shortly before the hour mark, despite the Blues enjoying most of the possession. Sol Gordon then created Harrison Bettoni’s 71st-minute goal before Chizaram Ezenwata drew us level in the closing stages. Freddy Bernal had kept Chelsea in the contest with several important saves and denied Jack Sparkes during the shoot-out, before Justin Osagie scored the decisive spot-kick to help us secure two points and go top in Southern Group C. Gordon had the first sight of goal after eight minutes, letting fly from the right side of the penalty area but sending his effort wide. Bernal produced a couple of important early saves to keep the contest close, but Bristol Rovers opened the scoring in the 22nd minute. Ryan de Havilland played the ball forward to Jack Aitchison, whose pass across goal was converted by Rijks. Chelsea had an opportunity to respond soon afterwards when Gordon won possession from Sparkes and found Ezenwata, but the forward was unable to take the chance. Harry Hudson made a double change in the 56th minute, introducing Lewi Richards and Mahdi Nicoll-Jazuli in place of Calvin Diakite and Harrison McMahon. Two minutes later, a cross the Blues were unable to clear reached Quigley at the far post and the striker finished to double the hosts’ advantage. Chelsea, who saw Andrew Pennie replace Jashayde Greenwood shortly after the hour mark, reduced the deficit in the 71st minute. Gordon beat Sparkes and drove to the byline before cutting the ball back for Bettoni, who finished first time. Bettoni found space again soon afterwards and went close to an equaliser. That second goal arrived in the 82nd minute. Nicoll-Jazuli’s neat spin created the opening and Ezenwata found the corner to bring the Blues level. Chelsea went in search of the winner and Pennie struck the side-netting in the second minute of stoppage time but the contest went to penalties. Ezenwata and Bettoni converted spot-kicks to help the Blues go 2-1 ahead, after Bernal saved from Sparkes. Richards then scored to make it 3-2 in the shootout and when Richard Smallwood failed to convert, it left Osagie to calmly seal a 4-2 shoot-out victory. Cobham Next Gen begin our EFL Trophy campaign with two points, earning one for the draw after 90 minutes and securing the bonus point through our shoot-out success. news.body_en: Three Chelsea players have been named in the PFA Women's Super League Team of the Year for the 2025/26 campaign, which was revealed at an awards ceremony at Manchester Opera House this evening. With the Blues preparing for tomorrow evening's UEFA Champions League qualifying round first leg against Real Sociedad – which can be viewed live on the Chelsea Official App and website – neither Sonia Bompastor nor her players attended the event. Yet that did not stop the performances of a trio of our players last season from being recognised by their fellow professionals. Hannah Hampton secured the goalkeeper spot in the Team of the Year, having kept eight clean sheets in 18 league appearances during the previous campaign. The PFA WSL Team of the Year in association with Care Fertility 🏆Voted for by the players. pic.twitter.com/94iUFmy5wA Fellow Blue and England international Lauren James was also handed a place in the side, having been voted by fans as our Player of the Season last year. Our No.10 scored several sublime goals last term, netting five times in 14 domestic games, and also went past the 100-appearance marker in blue. The third and final place in the WSL Team of the Year for a Chelsea player was Ellie Carpenter, who impressed throughout her maiden campaign in the English game. The Australian international made 19 appearances in the top flight last term, scoring twice and providing two assists. Several Blues received nominations for awards prior to Tuesday's ceremony. James was shortlisted for the PFA WSL Player of the Year honour, which went to Manchester City's Bunny Shaw, while Veerle Buurman and Alyssa Thompson were up for the PFA WSL Young Player of the Year. Be there to welcome our award-winners to our new home at Stamford Bridge when we take on Aston Villa in our first Women's Super League match of the season on 5 September at 12.35pm!

news.title: Key talking points from Bompastor and Bronze ahead of Real Sociedad
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor and Lucy Bronze faced the media at Cobham this afternoon ahead of our Women's Champions League qualifier clash against Real Sociedad on Wednesday night. The Blues are looking to gain an advantage in the first leg at home in our maiden match at the Cherry Red Records Stadium, before heading to Spain for the return leg on 2 September. Tickets are still available for Wednesday's game, and you can purchase them here. Alongside the latest injury news provided by Bompastor, here is a rundown of the other major talking points from today's press conference... Sonia Bompastor: It will be a strong test. Real Sociedad finished third in the Liga F. They are a Spanish team, so they have a really strong philosophy in possession, but they have a lot of quality out of possession as well. We know everything about them now, and we prepared for the game well. But the game tomorrow will also be about us, and I'm confident with the quality we have shown during pre-season. Lucy Bronze: I remember playing against Real Sociedad in Liga F when I was at Barcelona, and they were always a good team. They always played good football. We had good results against them, but I always remember them being a really good team, something that me and Keira (Walsh) both spoke about recently. I actually watched the game last year when they were playing against Barca. They defended really well, which isn't the easiest thing to do against Barca when they were continually attacking. SB: Pre-season has been really good. We have worked really hard with a lot of intensity in training sessions. We travelled all over the world, and it was a really good opportunity for the squad to be together and for us to get to know each other better. Since we came back, we also recovered really well from the travel, but we got back to business, and I think we are in a really good place for the game tomorrow. LB: We've got a lot of young, talented players at Chelsea, a lot of eager players who are keen to learn and to listen. Sometimes they get things wrong, but they try really hard, and it's exciting to be part of the club and to see so many players grow, develop and improve every day. I think that's the exciting part of this team this year: the youth and the exuberance we will have on the pitch. LB: I think it's fun. We like playing against teams from different countries. The league phase last year was different, and I guess this is just another difference, but we're very much focused on this game. We know it's very important for us to win tomorrow, especially playing at home. We don't take anything for granted. We know what a good team they are. I think having more games this year is exciting for us as Chelsea, and being in a different position just allows you to adapt and learn new things about the team. LB: People forget how much spotlight was put on her from a very young age. But I think in the team at Chelsea, you can see she feels comfortable. She's grown as a player. She's grown as a person. You can see that she's grown so many connections with all of the team. We all know that when LJ is flowing, there's nobody in the world that can stop her. So it's nice to see that she's growing a lot. SB: As a coach, I'm someone who really cares about the players, but as a human, I also care about the humans and the person. So I think in this environment, I always try my best to encourage the players to be themselves and to express themselves. It's okay for us to be vulnerable sometimes. We spend so much time together, so I'm happy with what Lucy said in terms of allowing people to be themselves, in terms of vulnerability, but also when they are showing confidence, it's something good. LB: Pre-season has gone so well. The new signings are fitting in really well too. It just feels like we're on a fresh start. We have kind of put a line in the sand from last season, and moving forward to be even bigger and better than Chelsea's ever been. Be there to welcome CFCW to our new home at Stamford Bridge when we take on Aston Villa in our first Women's Super League match of the season on 5 September at 12.35pm!

news.title: Rogers in focus 🔎
Analysis: How POTM Cole Palmer inspired Blues to victory
news.body_en: We detail the pivotal role Cole Palmer played in helping the Blues get our Premier League campaign up and running with a victory at Fulham. Our No10 was at his very best at Craven Cottage. Palmer assisted and scored a goal in the same Premier League game for the first time since February’s draw with Leeds United, with his cute finish early in the second half ultimately settling the contest. That was one of a game-high five attempts Palmer registered against Fulham, while he also led the way for successful dribbles (five), duels won (10), touches in the opposition box (nine) and fouls won (three). All those statistics point to the intent and confidence with which Palmer played. His nine attempted take-ons showed just how keen he was to beat his man, with one twisting and turning run in the second half nearly culminating in a special solo strike. Xabi Alonso’s system, using Palmer in a pocket alongside Morgan Rogers and off Joao Pedro, helped our No10 receive the ball. He spent more time in possession than every Chelsea outfielder bar Reece James, Josh Acheampong and Morgan Lacroix. Palmer was consistently effective when he had the ball at his feet. His assist for Joao Pedro’s record-breaking goal – the fastest ever scored in the Premier League on an opening weekend – was one of three key passes Palmer played, a figure bettered only by Rogers’ five. In total, Palmer completed 88 per cent of his passes, significantly higher than the team average of 82 per cent. A significant proportion (14) were played in the final third, too, highlighting his willingness to take risks. The weight and direction of Palmer’s passes were pivotal to our first and second goals, while his own strike showed his pinpoint accuracy in front of goal. The angle was narrow, so he aimed to slip the ball through Bernd Leno’s legs – and succeeded. Palmer wasn’t afraid to do his defensive work, either. He won two tackles and recovered possession seven times, including on three occasions in the final third. Those high turnovers proved instrumental for our first two goals of the night. Palmer was ably assisted by Joao Pedro and Rogers. That trio played 20 passes between them and showed signs of an understanding that bodes very well for the future – as does Palmer’s elite display. news.title: Bompastor & Bronze Press Conference 🎙️
Bompastor confirms injured Chelsea trio to miss Real Sociedad game
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor has confirmed she will be without the services of three players for the first leg of our Champions League qualifying tie against Real Sociedad. The Blues head coach was joined by Lucy Bronze on Tuesday afternoon to answer the media’s questions ahead of our opening fixture of the 2026/27 campaign, which takes place at the Cherry Red Records Stadium in Wimbledon. It will be streamed for free live on the Chelsea Official App and website. Bompastor will hope to see her side establish a lead ahead of the second leg in Spain next week, but she will not be able to call upon Erin Cuthbert, Mayra Ramirez and Manaka Matsukubo. ‘We have a squad with almost everyone pretty available from pre-season,’ said Bompastor. ‘The ones who are not available are Erin Cuthbert, who had an injury in the last international break and she's recovering from that. We also have Manaka, who won't be available for this game, and Mayra as well, who won't be available for the game. ‘I don't think we could expect to see them for the second leg. I think it'll be a little bit longer, but it's difficult to put a timeframe on it. They are working really well and progressing as we want them to progress, but yeah, no timeframe. ‘Except from these three, everyone else is available.’ Bompastor expanded on Ramirez’s recovery following the serious hamstring injury she suffered this time last year, with the head coach explaining her absence on Wednesday is expected. ‘Mayra is recovering from not having played last season, and I think it's tough sometimes when you haven't played for the full season to be ready to compete. ‘It's part of her rehab plan. She's not quite ready, but we are working closely with her to make sure she returns on the pitch as fit as possible.’

news.title: Joao Pedro on joining Palmer and Rogers in a ‘special’ front three
news.body_en: Joao Pedro believes Chelsea showed our strength in an impressive opening game of what could be a great season for the Blues, especially with the Brazilian lining up alongside Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers in a new-look attack. The starting line-up for Xabi Alonso’s first competitive match as Chelsea manager featured a front three of Joao Pedro down the middle, supported either side by Palmer and summer signing Rogers. It proved a big hit on its first outing, with all three of those players getting on the scoresheet as we began our 2026/27 campaign with a 3-2 Premier League win away at neighbours Fulham on Monday evening. That front three is already causing plenty of excitement among the Blues supporters following its debut at Craven Cottage, and it seems to be shared by Joao Pedro after a performance full of movement and clever combinations. ‘Cole and Morgan, they are special players. Everyone knows that,’ said Joao Pedro after Chelsea’s winning start to the season. ‘I'm very grateful to play with them because I know if I make some runs, like yesterday, you know Cole and Morgan are going to give the ball to me, and I have to be ready to score. So it's very special for me to play with them. ‘I just try to enjoy and try to help my team in every game. Then this season, see what I get. I just try to score in every opportunity I have. ‘I’ve known Morgan since a long time ago because we played against each other,' added our new number nine. 'So when he joined the club, I knew it was very good for us because he's a very good player, and I think he can help us like he did yesterday. ‘I think now in the game, if we move a lot, it will be difficult for defenders to pick up one player, to stay with them. The manager led us to be free on the pitch, so we understand each other well. So this just helps us and hopefully it can happen many more times this season.’ The striker was quick to point out the victory was down to the whole team’s display, though, not just that of the front three. Furthermore, he believes it was a performance and result which laid down a marker for the season to come. ‘I think the whole group was very good, we tried to do our job,’ he continued. ‘We conceded two goals, but I think we did a great game. It's very difficult to play there and get the three points, and that is the important thing. ‘I think it's too early to say what our target is, but we need to go step-by-step. We have to focus on the Premier League and the cups. We have a lot of time to train as well, to know what the coach wants from us. Let's see in the end, hopefully we can achieve our targets. ‘I will enjoy this season, of course, because I think we can achieve higher things. When you play for Chelsea, you always need to look for that. Yesterday was a great game to show our power and hopefully we can continue like this in the rest of the season.’ Up next is our midweek Carabao Cup clash against Luton Town and Alonso's Premier League home debut against Brighton & Hove Albion. news.title: Alonso explains how Palmer, Joao Pedro and Rogers can lead and inspire
news.body_en: Fulham discovered exactly what the attacking trio Cole Palmer, Joao Pedro and Morgan Rogers of are capable of at Craven Cottage on Monday evening. It was far less of a surprise for Blues manager Xabi Alonso, who believes the trio can inspire their Chelsea team-mates throughout the campaign. Palmer’s qualities are well known to Chelsea supporters; the 24-year-old has showcased them throughout his time at Stamford Bridge. Joao Pedro, who scored 20 goals and was named Player of the Season, has also demonstrated his talents on countless occasions. Rogers’ addition came earlier this summer and he has needed little time to adapt to life at Chelsea. Alonso deployed the three from the start against Fulham. Within 31 seconds, Palmer had teed up Joao Pedro to open the scoring. Rogers then opened his account in blue – sweeping home after good work from fellow signing Maxence Lacroix – and Joao Pedro returned the favour in the second period for Palmer, who netted his first of the campaign from an acute angle. Their goals proved decisive, with the Blues coming away from our west London neighbours with a 3-2 victory. And Alonso, while insisting he would not construct a team around the trio, emphasised what Palmer, Joao Pedro and Rogers can bring to the Chelsea side. He said: ‘They are going to be a very important part, but to build around them, no, it’s to build a team with them. They need to take responsibility, they need to lead the rest, they need to inspire the rest, because if they do great, the others will follow. 'We need to use them in the best possible situations and we need to have good links to reach them and they need to help the team be solid. The three of them, they have played for the team and scored, and that’s always important for the forwards.’ Palmer’s display on the banks of the Thames was particularly encouraging. For much of the previous campaign, he struggled with injury. It inhibited his game, with the England international admitting he wasn’t sure from one day to the next whether he would be in discomfort. Yet against Fulham, having had the summer off, Palmer appeared back to his fluid best. He weaved effortlessly beyond challenges and, while scoring and fashioning chances for team-mates, was also hugely impressive without the ball. Naturally, Alonso was pleased for the Blues’ No.10, and highlighted the influence Palmer can have when enjoying his football. He said: ‘I am very happy for Cole because I have really enjoyed seeing him play with this dynamism, with this freedom, with this responsibility, helping the team, and feeling important. We need that for the team. If Cole feels this way, we will have a better team and a better Chelsea. 'I am happy for him that he enjoyed his game, and you can see that.’ Up next is our midweek Carabao Cup clash against Luton Town and Alonso's Premier League home debut against Brighton & Hove Albion. news.title: Morgan Rogers: An enjoyable debut!
news.body_en: As debuts go, that Chelsea one from Morgan Rogers wasn’t half bad. After his switch to Stamford Bridge from Aston Villa, the England international would have been itching to hit the ground running. So scoring and helping the Blues to victory over Fulham will certainly have helped. Our No.17 restored our lead at Craven Cottage, after Joshua King had cancelled out Joao Pedro’s opener – which came after just 32 seconds. Cole Palmer, a close friend of Rogers, made it 3-1 just after the break, before Gonzalo Garcia reduced the deficit for Fulham. In the end, the Blues took all three points and Rogers – who played a key role alongside Palmer in a number ten role for Xabi Alonso’s side – believes this victory was a good start, but just that: a start. He believes there are still many gears for us to go up. ‘It was a great game to play in,’ Rogers said with a beaming smile. ‘Obviously to score and help the team win, that’s everything that I wanted from a debut. ‘I thought the quality of our play was excellent and it was so enjoyable out there. Fulham is a difficult place to come to, and they played really well, but we had that fight, that grit and I think we were the better team on the night. ‘For me, we deserved the win and I’m really happy with how the game went.’ Rogers would have been keen to make an impression at his new club, following his summer switch from Aston Villa, and having arrived later than some of his team-mates due to his involvement at the World Cup, the attacker believes the best version of him is still to come. ‘I didn’t feel that sharp towards the end, I was a bit tired and that’s why I came off for the last 10 minutes,’ admitted Morgan. ‘I’ve felt really good in pre-season but I’ve not had much of a break due to the World Cup, so I wanted to keep myself fresh. ‘Coming to a new team, you don't want to come in sluggish and off the pace, so I tried to keep myself in the best shape as possible and I’ve tried to get up to speed as quickly as I can. ‘I still think there are more gears to go, and I've got to try and find them as quickly as possible because the games are coming thick and fast. ‘But as I said, I felt good out there and I enjoyed it.’ Up next is our midweek Carabao Cup clash against Luton Town and Xabi Alonso's Premier League home debut against Brighton & Hove Albion. news.title: OTD: Torres ingenuity against Newcastle!
Highlights: Fulham 2-3 Chelsea
Extended: Fulham 2-3 Chelsea
Full match: Fulham vs Chelsea
'I could feel the excitement'
Rogers' speaks after debut win
Alonso: 'A very professional, solid performance with maturity'
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso believes his Chelsea side produced a ‘very professional, solid performance with maturity’ to defeat Fulham in our Premier League opener and send the Chelsea supporters home from Craven Cottage with ‘happy faces’. Our first top-flight match of the campaign didn’t disappoint, with the west London derby against our neighbours testing the Blues in a variety of different ways. We broke the deadlock after just 32 seconds when Cole Palmer flicked a pass to Joao Pedro, who produced a deft finish to put us ahead. Fulham hit back midway through the opening period via Josh King, but Alonso’s side went into the interval ahead when Morgan Rogers struck on his debut. Cole Palmer then netted soon after the restart and, despite Fulham pulling a goal back through Gonzalo Garcia, we held on to claim all three points. After our win, Alonso highlighted several areas for improvement for his side. Yet the Chelsea manager was pleased to start his tenure with a win that showcased many different qualities we will need throughout the season ahead. ‘It feels very good, for sure,’ Alonso said in his post-match press conference. ‘We know how tough it is to win any Premier League game, and any away Premier League game. We prepared for an intense game, and I feel it was a very professional, solid performance, showing maturity and managing the difficult moments. ‘We got the lead quite early, had chances to score the second one, but after the equaliser we were through ten minutes when we didn’t choose the right moments to press and the movements. 'We corrected this well and in the second half, we felt comfortable without the ball, controlling the game. It was a performance to build for the future. There are things to improve for sure, but it was a good first day.’ Alonso added: ‘[It’s important] to manage in difficult moments, not to lose this emotional control. We know the Premier League is fantastic because sometimes the games are out of your hands. 'You don’t control them, so the players on the pitch need to know how to manage it – it’s as important as the tactics being right. It’s a process but today we went through good moments on that and we need to carry on that.’ After the full-time whistle was blown at Craven Cottage, Alonso and his players made their way over to the Chelsea faithful who had made the short trip down the Fulham Road to support their side. The Spaniard believes such moments are important in building a connection between those on the pitch and those in the stands. He said: ‘We are happy to play our first Premier League game of the season. My first official Premier League game with Chelsea felt great; in this stadium with our fans at the end, celebrating with them. ‘I had the feeling before kick-off that they were excited and they were hoping to see a good performance from the team, a serious one, and one they could see that we gave everything and fought for everything. I saw happy faces in the end and it’s important to create this bond. It’s early days, first game, but a good one.’

news.title: Match gallery: Off to a winning start!
Match report: Fulham 2-3 Chelsea
news.body_en: Joao Pedro, Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer all got on the scoresheet as Xabi Alonso's first game in charge of Chelsea ended in a 3-2 victory over west London neighbours Fulham at Craven Cottage. We made the ideal start to a half in which momentum swung back and forth. After just 32 seconds, Palmer flicked a pass into the path of Joao Pedro, who broke clear of the Fulham backline to score. Fulham equalised via Josh King in the 23rd minute, but Alonso's side responded and deservedly went into the interval ahead when, after excellent work from Maxence Lacroix, Rogers swept home on his debut. Palmer got his name on the scoresheet early into the second half, finishing off an attack which included contributions from Rogers and Joao Pedro. Yet Fulham hit back quickly through Gonzalo Garcia. The Blues had to dig in during the time that remained. It was about grit and determination – and we came through to ensure a winning start for Alonso and to our Premier League campaign. Marco Palestra and Moises Caicedo both missed the game with minor setbacks. So Alonso opted for a starting XI of Robert Sanchez, Josh Acheampong, Maxence Lacroix, Levi Colwill, Malo Gusto, captain Reece James, Romeo Lavia, Jorrel Hato, Palmer, Rogers and Joao Pedro. Alonso anticipated a fiery west London derby – and the game lived up to his expectations. Yet we made the perfect start at Craven Cottage, with our opening goal arriving inside 35 seconds. There appeared little danger when a Fulham clearance was fired into the Chelsea half, but Lacroix won his header, the ball broke to Palmer, who flicked it deftly into the path of Joao Pedro. The Brazilian's first touch set him free of the Fulham defence and he lifted a fine finish over Leno. The goal was an instant settler and enabled the Blues attackers to begin expressing themselves. Rogers and Palmer linked neatly throughout the opening period and fashioned chances. The former saw a powerful shot blocked from the edge of the area; the latter forced Bernd Leno into a near-post save with a powerful drive. As the half progressed, Fulham started to wrestle momentum their way. King forced Sanchez into a smart reaction stop and, from the resulting corner, Cesar Palacios fired harmlessly over the crossbar. The home side did manage to pull level midway through the opening 45 minutes, as a neat exchange of passes down the Blues' left flank enabled King to break into the penalty area and drill a shot beyond Sanchez. A reaction was needed from Alonso's side. It quickly came. After seeing off a spell of Fulham pressure, we created several opportunities. Joao Pedro had the first, volleying a Palmer cross narrowly wide, before James tested Leno following a blocked Rogers shot. Lavia was next to be thwarted by the Fulham goalkeeper, who reacted well to deny the Belgian midfielder from close range following a well-worked short corner by the Blues. Deservedly, our efforts were eventually rewarded four minutes before the interval. After collecting possession on the half-turn, Palmer slipped a pass to Lacroix, who did excellently to trick his way beyond Jorge Cuenca and cross from the byline. The ball raced across the Fulham penalty area into the path of fellow summer signing Rogers, who swept home a finish to score on his Blues debut. There was time before the interval to push for a third, and the vibrant Palmer came close with a curled attempt from 20 yards that whistled narrowly wide. Yet, importantly, we went in ahead. Alonso will not have wanted his side to let up – the game felt in our hands – and Palmer picked up from where he left off in the opening period. One sublime run, in which he skipped beyond multiple challenges, almost enabled the Blues' No.10 to guide a finish into the far post. But moments later, there was no mistake. Our third goal started with Sanchez, who drove a pass forward toward Rogers. The England international flicked a header onto Joao Pedro, who bound into the Fulham half, waited for an overlap from Palmer and slipped in his fellow attacker. Palmer assessed his options, which were minimal, and opted to guide a shot between the legs of Leno. The Fulham goalkeeper was beaten, and the Blues had a third goal. Yet, as in the first half, Fulham pulled themselves back into the game by quickly reducing the deficit. The Blues didn't deal with a long ball forward and Timothy Castagne collected and fired a shot toward goal. Sanchez saved, but the rebound fell to Garcia, who reacted well to head home. The game became less frenetic as it progressed, with Alonso's side gaining greater control. It meant chances were harder to come by, although Joao Pedro did fire over an attempt from distance. With 25 minutes to play, the Blues manager turned to his bench. Pep Chavarria was introduced for his Blues debut for Hato, while Enzo Fernandez replaced Lavia. As the minutes ticked down, Fulham pushed hard for an equaliser. King came close again with another low effort that this time fizzed beyond the post, before a long ball forward presented Antonee Robinson with an opportunity to lob Sanchez. However, the USA international guided his attempt wide. With eight minutes remaining, Alonso made two more changes. Geovany Quenda and Estevao Willian were brought on; Rogers and Palmer were replaced. Sanchez had to stay alert in the closing stages, and the Blues goalkeeper reacted well to deny substitute Ryan Sessegnon at his near post. Four minutes of additional time were added. Yet just before they were entered, we had the ball in the back of the net. Quenda had a shot saved by Leno and Joao Pedro turned home the rebound, but the Portuguese winger was offside in the build-up. It mattered not, as Alonso's side saw out the contest to ensure we started the season with a victory and three points. It's a quick turnaround for the Blues, as we return to action on Thursday evening in the Carabao Cup, with League One Luton Town visiting Stamford Bridge. news.title: Xabi Alonso explains Marco Palestra and Moises Caicedo absences against Fulham
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso has confirmed why Chelsea duo Marco Palestra and Moises Caicedo are not in the matchday squad for our Premier League opener against Fulham. Our top-flight campaign begins a stone’s throw away from Stamford Bridge, with Alonso’s first competitive game as Chelsea manager taking place at Craven Cottage, the home of our west London neighbours. The Spaniard has named a starting XI that includes Robert Sanchez, Josh Acheampong, Maxence Lacroix, Levi Colwill, Malo Gusto, Reece James, Romeo Lavia, Jorrel Hato, Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro, but the absence of Palestra and Caicedo is noteworthy. Alonso faced the media pre-game and was asked why the duo missed out. He replied: ‘They had minor setbacks during the week, so they were not fit to play tonight. New faces debut for us, Morgan and Max, and they are going to play important roles through the year.’ After a pre-season campaign that saw matches played in Australia and Asia, in addition to a friendly against Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge, Alonso gets the chance to oversee a game which has points at stake. And the new Blues manager is looking forward to the contest. He said: 'Everyone is excited in the building and in the team. It’s great that after a long pre-season we are where we want to be. First Premier League game and I’m really happy to be involved. 'It’s going to be emotional for everyone, given it’s our first game. It’s a derby and the excitement of the crowd will be there. So we will need to manage the game.'

Lola Brown: My journey to Chelsea
news.body_en: When you talk to Chelsea Academy graduate Lola Brown, it’s difficult to believe that she’s still only 18. She speaks with maturity well beyond her years, but still has a youthful glint in her eye. It’s clear she’s hungry, and with a calm head to match, she’s ideally placed to soak up everything she needs to learn from the senior professionals at Chelsea. That, alongside her natural ability on the pitch, means the reasons for offering Brown a three-year contract extension are evident. During the domestic Treble-winning campaign of 2024/25, she made her senior debut for the Blues, and after a loan spell at Crystal Palace last season, she’s loving life back in SW6. ‘Football means absolutely everything to me,’ she smiles. ‘When you wake up in the morning, you have something to strive towards. It's always given me a purpose, and I'm also very competitive, so it drives me to want to win. ‘It’s more than just the matchday, though. It's the day-to-day. Every single day you're going for something. That’s why it means everything.’ Perhaps part of the reason for Brown’s mature outlook is the experience of a childhood spent on foreign shores. She began her school life in Malta, where she remained until the age of eight, before her parents returned to England. Two years later, the youngster secured a place in the Chelsea Academy. ‘My parents just went over to Malta, sort of like a getaway,’ she explains. ‘They went for two years, but ended up staying for 14 because they loved it so much. I was born there and then lived there till I was eight. I actually absolutely loved it there. Malta is a massive part of who I am; it’s where I grew up. I owe a lot to Malta, in terms of my early stages and making me who I am as a person. ‘My whole family loves sports. We were all really competitive and driven when I was young, which massively shaped me as a person. The people I had around me in those early years really embedded good morals that I want to live by. ‘I always played football with my brother in the garden in Malta. He’s six years older than me, but when I'd beat him 1-v-1, he'd just pick me up! I would get a bit annoyed because I'm not sure that's part of the rules... ‘At the age of four or five I started playing football at school. My school coach also ran the team in Malta, so then I joined a boys' team pretty soon afterwards. I started school in Malta, then we moved to England. ‘When I came over here, I joined another boys’ team, and I played with them for a while, too,' adds Lola. 'I joined the Academy at Under-12 level, but I was only 10. I was playing against Chelsea with my boys’ team, and that's where they picked me up. Playing on a boys' team is always hard, but I also think it helped me to grow. I enjoyed the challenge.’ They say it takes a village to raise a child, and it’s certainly the same when it comes to developing a young footballer into a professional. Brown credits Leanne Champ at the Chelsea Academy and is also grateful to her family for the sacrifices they made when she was growing up as a young footballer. ‘Leanne helped me throughout the whole Academy,’ Brown continues. ‘She helped me progress as a player and developed my confidence. ‘It was all worth it when I signed my first professional contract two years ago. It was massive. I think that's when you realise it's more than just football. So many people have sacrificed so much for you to get to that moment. ‘My mum massively helped me to get where I am today. She would drive me literally every day. I lived far away, so it'd be like a four-hour round trip every single day. Mum did the driving, but even my siblings were at home making dinner for themselves so I could live my dream. It means so much. Still only 18, Brown can remember looking up to Chelsea players past and present. One of those heroes – Lucy Bronze – is now her Blues team-mate, a dream scenario for the enthusiastic young player. She recalls watching Bronze score the winner for Manchester City in the 2016 Women’s League Cup final. Brown even walked out alongside Willian as a mascot at Stamford Bridge before making her debut on the same pitch a few years later, with a few wise words in her ear from head coach Sonia Bompastor. ‘My two heroes were Bronze and Fran Kirby when I was growing up,’ she says. ‘A match that always comes into mind was my first ever women's match I went to, and I saw Lucy Bronze score a header in a final. I was a pretty big fan. Now I’m playing with her, which is a bit surreal. I felt a bit like that with Fran Kirby as well because she was here for a bit when I trained with her, and I’d always idolised her. ‘My debut against Celtic in the Champions League was so surreal, especially because it was at Stamford Bridge. I remember warming up and looking at the pitch, because it was the first time I'd been on it except for when I was really young as a mascot. I walked out with Willian on that day. ‘Even when I was warming up, I was thinking, "Oh, I could actually come on here at Stamford Bridge." So when I got subbed on, I was just super excited. The nerves disappeared, and it was more just excitement to get on the pitch. ‘I think Sonia said to enjoy it and take in the moment and to be brave and confident on the pitch.’ Wise words indeed for a player who has her whole future ahead of her and is here to stay at Chelsea.

news.title: Lola Brown signs new contract
news.body_en: Chelsea midfielder Lola Brown has put pen to paper on a new contract, committing her future to the club until at least 2029. Having joined the Blues during the 2019/20 season, she agreed her first professional contract in November 2024, aged 17. On signing her new deal, Brown said: ‘It feels amazing. I’m super proud. It’s a club I always wanted to sign a professional contract with, so to sign my second one is an amazing feeling. ‘Chelsea have developed me from a young age, and I can see how much I have developed here and how much I continue to develop. ‘Being around this environment and learning from the best helps you progress as a player. Now I want to win as many trophies as possible, and on a personal level I want to score my first professional goal as a Chelsea player.’ Brown was named Chelsea Women’s Academy Under-18 Player of the Year for the 2023/24 campaign. The teenager made her senior debut for the club the following season, coming on against Celtic in the Women’s Champions League group stage. She earned further minutes in a win over Twente, and towards the end of that domestic Treble-winning campaign, made her WSL debut in a victory at Tottenham. A loan move was next on the agenda for Brown as she moved across London to join Crystal Palace in WSL2. An injury hampered her progress in the first half of the campaign, but she returned to action in January and played a key role in the Eagles’ promotion back to the top flight. Palace went into a key clash with Portsmouth knowing that a win would guarantee automatic promotion. With the scores level at half-time, Brown was brought on and provided three assists to help secure an eventual 6-1 victory. She was voted the Player of the Match for her efforts. On the international stage, Brown has represented England at Under-16, Under-17, Under-19 and Under-20 levels, and has been called up to the Young Lionesses squad for September's U-20 Women's World Cup.

news.title: Cesar Azpilicueta: The Chelsea player who won it all
news.body_en: On the anniversary of Chelsea legend Cesar Azpilicueta joining the club, we reflect on the Spaniard's 11 trophy-laden years as a Blues player. Azpilicueta recently announced he was hanging up his boots at the end of a long and distinguished career, which included more than a decade with Chelsea. Throughout his time at Stamford Bridge, Azpilicueta stepped up to whatever challenge was put in front of him. No matter the position, the formation or the head coach, the Spaniard was always an integral part of the team. When Azpilicueta first arrived ahead on August 24 2012, the then 23-year-old faced a tough task breaking into the side with Ashley Cole and Branislav Ivanovic well-established in the full-back roles and Chelsea champions of Europe after that famous night in Munich. However, Azpilicueta went from strength to strength over the course of the campaign after making his debut in a 6-0 home win over Wolverhampton Wanderers in the League Cup. He became an almost ever-present at right-back in the latter months of the season and played the full 90 minutes in all but one of our UEFA Europa League games en route to glory in Amsterdam. Ivanovic was Jose Mourinho’s preferred option on the right of defence early into the campaign that followed, although Azpilicueta’s first start of 2013/14 – a 2-0 League Cup win at Arsenal – did bring his first goal for the club. Cesar’s versatility was soon demonstrated, however, following an injury to Cole. After a fine performance at left-back against Schalke in the UEFA Champions League, he made the spot his own, a situation which did not change even after Cole returned to fitness. Azpilicueta had forced his way into his manager’s plans and contributed immensely to the Premier League’s best defensive record – we conceded just 27 times in 38 games. As a result, Azpilicueta was named our Players’ Player of the Year. He remained the first choice left-back despite the signing of Filipe Luis ahead of the 2014/15 season. Once again, Azpilicueta was a vital member of the team as the first league title of his career was sealed. He made 29 top-flight appearances as well as helping us keep a clean sheet in a League Cup final win over Tottenham Hotspur. The defender’s first Premier League goal for Chelsea earned a 3-2 win over West Bromwich Albion early in the next season, before he reverted to his natural position on the right of our backline under Guus Hiddink in 2015/16. Another change of role followed as Azpilicueta was used on the right of Antonio Conte’s three-man defence, which he implemented early into his tenure at Stamford Bridge. Azpilicueta excelled as an impressive run of clean sheets contributed to a club-record sequence of wins. He would go on to play in every minute of every league game in our title-winning 2016/17 season, only the fourth outfield player ever to do so for a victorious Premier League side. And it was his assist for Michy Batshuayi’s goal at West Brom which ultimately secured that status for Chelsea. Azpilicueta’s leadership qualities were also coming to the fore. He captained Chelsea on 21 occasions in 2017/18, in addition to enjoying his best campaign to that point from an attacking point of view. He scored three goals and set up plenty more, particularly through his excellent understanding with Alvaro Morata. But it was his defensive prowess on show in a clean sheet at Wembley as we beat Manchester United in the FA Cup final. Returning to right-back in Maurizio Sarri’s side, Azpilicueta made more appearances than any other Blues player for the third successive campaign, culminating in leading the team out in Baku for our 2019 Europa League final win over Arsenal. His only goal of the season, a late equaliser at Cardiff City, turned out to be a crucial one in the top-four race. His status as captain was made permanent following the departure of Gary Cahill in 2019 and Azpilicueta’s versatility would prove vital in his first campaign as full-time skipper, featuring in four different positions as Frank Lampard frequently shifted formations. His experience played a big part when football returned following a hiatus during the Covid-19 pandemic. Azpi played every minute for the remainder of the Premier League as we homed in on Champions League qualification, although his presence was missed when an injury forced him off with the scores tied 1-1 in our FA Cup final defeat to Arsenal. The emergence of Reece James meant Azpi’s opportunities were limited in the first half of 2020/21, even if his selfless attitude meant he was still an important figure, helping to guide a youthful squad full of potential but light on experience. However, he was straight into the starting line-up after the arrival of Thomas Tuchel and provided the first goal of our new head coach’s reign by scoring the opener in a 2-0 win against Burnley. A season which had started with the ever-resilient Azpilicueta on the fringes would end with arguably his greatest moment at Chelsea. Switching between playing on the right of a back three and at wing-back, he missed just three games in all competitions for Tuchel, leading by example in big games to produce some of his best performances for the club. He became only the second Chelsea captain to lift the Champions League trophy after we beat Manchester City in the final in Porto, one late defensive block to preserve our clean sheet epitomising his commitment to the cause. His contribution was recognised as one of four Blues named on the 30-man shortlist for the 2021 Ballon d’Or. Azpilicueta’s penultimate season at Stamford Bridge underlined his status as one the most successful Chelsea players of all time, as he captained us to two more trophies in the form of the UEFA Super Cup and, for the first time in our history, the FIFA Club World Cup. He completed his own clean sweep of major silverware in the process. Those trophy successes were followed by a major landmark as Azpi captained the side for the 200th time, in a 1-1 Premier League draw with Manchester United in April, five years after he had first worn the armband, at Wembley in a 4-2 FA Cup semi-final win over Tottenham. Azpilicueta passed the 500-game mark in his last season at Chelsea. He left the club having made more appearances than any other overseas player in our history. Indeed, only five Blues have featured more for Chelsea, and he rightly joins Ron Harris, Peter Bonetti, John Terry, Frank Lampard and John Hollins on the list of true club legends. Departed, retired, but never forgotten. The Chelsea player who really did win it all.

news.title: Fulham vs Chelsea: All you need to know
news.body_en: A west London derby kicks off Chelsea’s league campaign for the first time in our history with the short trip down the river for Monday’s 8pm fixture at Fulham. This will be the fourth time the Blues’ season opens on the first day of the week – we won each of the previous three at Burnley (2014/15), home to West Ham (2016/17) and away to Brighton (2020/21). Two of those became title-winning seasons and the other ended in Champions League glory. Overall, Chelsea have won eleven of the past 14 Premier League matches played on a Monday. The World champions have also taken three points from four of the past five all-capital clashes in the top flight. Chelsea’s new manager Xabi Alonso and his Cottagers counterpart Alvaro Arbeloa have much in common. They both managed Real Madrid in 2025/26 and were Liverpool team-mates in nine historic games against the Blues, losing four and drawing three. This is the first time any manager’s Premier League bow has come against a former team-mate in that competition. The Blues’ 2-1 loss on the bank of the Thames was one of many affected by red cards last season – Marc Cucurella receiving his marching orders for denying a goalscoring opportunity after just 22 minutes. One legacy of that unhappy collection of red and yellow cards is that Wes Fofana is suspended for our opening two fixtures. 22 Man United20 Chelsea = Arsenal17 Man City16 Liverpool Chelsea have started the Premier League season with a London derby five times without defeat. A highlight of the 4-2 home win against West Ham in 2000 was a spectacular debut goal from distance by Mario Stanic, while the 3-2 at Charlton is remembered as much for red-carded Paul Konchesky’s elbow as the visitors’ Gianfranco Zola-inspired comeback and Frank Lampard’s coup de grace. The Hammers were beaten again in 2016, ushering in what would be a title-winning season under Antonio Conte. This time it was Diego Costa’s turn to settle the outcome in a 2-1 win. In 2021 Crystal Palace were the victims of a 3-0 pounding at the Bridge, Trevoh Chalobah among the goalscorers with his first for the Blues. When the same opponents rolled up in west London as FA Cup and Community Shield-winners last season, the run of wins in derby openers ended with an uneventful goalless draw. So far, all-capital clashes have accounted for 14 starts to a Chelsea league campaign. Back in 1957 at White Hart Lane, 17-year-old Jimmy Greaves made an auspicious scoring debut against Tottenham. In 1984, the Blues’ long-awaited return to the top tier was marked with an opener at Arsenal and John Neal’s newly-promoted side shared the spoils thanks to Kerry Dixon’s volleyed equaliser. - This is Chelsea's 35th campaign in the Premier League, and we are one of just six ever-present clubs in the competition. - Twenty-seven Chelsea players have scored a Premier League debut goal, most recently Christopher Nkunku at Wolves in December 2023. - The Blues have failed to win the opening Premier League game in each of the past three seasons (two draws, one loss). - However, the World champions have won six of the last eight league meetings at Craven Cottage, Fulham two. - Alonso’s first fixture outside London will be at Everton on 17 October – we will play at least seven matches across the capital before then. - Ten years ago Chelsea finished tenth in the Premier League with no European qualification but went on to win the title the following season, 2016/17. - Three Blues managers (Jose Mourinho, Carlo Ancelotti and Conte) have won the Premier League title during their debut season in charge – more than any other club. - The transfer window will close on Tuesday 1 September at 11pm UK time. - The building of the River Thames embankment near Craven Cottage stadium was carried out by contractors working for the Mears family out of Crabtree Wharf. The Mears family were later founding members of Chelsea FC.

news.title: Summer transfers 2026: All the Chelsea ins, outs and new contracts so far
news.body_en: With the 2026 summer transfer window now open, we keep you updated with all the deals done so far this summer... Versatile midfielder Barco arrived from Strasbourg, signing a contract until 2033. He has previous experience of English football with Brighton. The 29-year-old Spaniard joined Chelsea early in August following four seasons with Rayo Vallecano. The experienced England international joined the Blues in August after leaving Brentford, agreeing a two-year deal at Stamford Bridge. Lacroix made the short journey from Crystal Palace to Chelsea towards the end of July, fresh from his involvement for France at the 2026 World Cup. Lacroix's deal lasts until 2032. The Italian international became our first signing of the summer when he joined on a permanent deal from Atalanta at the start of July. Palestra signed a contract through to 2033. The winger's move to Chelsea was first confirmed in March 2025, before officially completing his move from Sporting Lisbon this summer. The Portuguese teenager signed a contract until 2034. England international Morgan Rogers signed from Aston Villa in July 2026, penning a contract until 2033. He has played 22 times for the Three Lions, including at this summer's World Cup, and established himself as one of the top attacking talents in the Premier League. Dastan Satpayev completed a transfer to Chelsea after his 18th birthday, having been a part of our pre-season tour in Australia and Asia. He subsequently joined Burnley on loan. Joining from Brighton and Hove Albion, where he had impressed in recent seasons, striker Welbeck became our fifth signing of the summer. His contract runs to 2028. 18-year-old Bettoni joined from Wigan Athletic on a contract until 2030. The attacking midfielder featured 27 times for the Latics last season, scoring four goals. Osborne, 18, joined from Hearts in Scotland and put pen to paper on a contract with the Blues until 2030. Toby Bell signed his first professional contract. The goalkeeper made his Under-18 debut in November 2024 and has represented England throughout his development pathway. The young winger commited his long-term future to Chelsea by signing a new contract until 2032, shortly before agreeing a loan switch to swap London for Lisbon in the 2026/27 season with a spell at Sporting. Academy attacker Sol Gordon signed a new contract until 2029. Having joined Chelsea's development centre at Under-8 level, Gordon has progressed through the Academy ranks to become a regular for our Under-18s and has also featured for the Blues' Under-21s. Academy striker Jashayde Greenwood signed his first professional contract with the club following his 17th birthday and after a successful maiden campaign at Chelsea. Harrison, an Academy midfielder who established himself as a regular for our Under-21s last season as we lifted the Premier League 2 title, signed a new contract until 2029. He later joined Wimbledon on loan. Our midfielder signed his first professional contract with the Blues following his 17th birthday. He has been with our Academy since Under-8s level. Academy defender Osagie signed a new contract keeping him at the club until 2029. He established himself as an important member of our Under-21 side last season. Ahead of the campaign starting, Joao Pedro signed a new contract with Chelsea until 2034. The Brazilian netted 20 goals in his debut season at the Bridge and was voted our Player of the Year. Before joining Dulwich Hamlet on loan, Academy goalkeeper Sands signed a new three-year contract. After captaining Chelsea Under-18s to victory in the Under-18 Premier League national final in 2026, the centre-back signed his first professional contract with the Blues. The 19-year-old Academy player embarked on his first loan in August 2026, joining Ligue 1 side Strasbourg for the forthcoming campaign. The defender, who has played 71 times for the Blues, joined Napoli on loan for the season. The Argentina international joined Aston Villa on loan for 2026/27 having scored eight goals in 43 appearances in his first season at Stamford Bridge. Academy midfielder Harrison signed for League One side AFC Wimbledon for the season, embarking on his maiden loan away from the Bridge. The goalkeeper has moved to Strasbourg on loan for the season. The 17-year-old winger departed on his maiden loan spell in the senior game, signing for Portsmouth ahead of the Championship season starting. Young goalkeeper Max Merrick embarked on his third loan away from the Bridge by joining Hartlepool United of the National League for the season. He has been in our first team matchday squad on 11 occasions in recent years. Chelsea Academy defender Murray-Campbell, who made his senior Blues debut against Shamrock Rovers in the 2024/25 UEFA Conference League, will spend the coming season gaining further experience of men's football with KV Kortrijk in the Belgian first division. The defender has joined Notts County of League One for the 2026/27 campaign, following his loan spell with Swansea City last term. The young goalkeeper signed a new contract until 2029 and joined non-league side Dulwich Hamlet on a youth loan. After completing his transfer to Chelsea, the Kazakh attacker moved to Burnley on loan for the season. Walsh, who played four games for our senior team in 2025 including as a 16-year-old, will spend the season on loan at Wigan Athletic in League One this season. Wilson embarked on his first loan in senior football in July 2026, joining newly-promoted League Two side Rochdale for the forthcoming campaign. The winger left for Ipswich Town after a season playing for our Academy sides. Chalobah completed a permanent transfer to Como in August, bringing his time as a Chelsea player to an end after nearly two decades with the Blues. He won four trophies, having established himself in our first team ahead of the 2021/22 campaign. The Spaniard left for Real Madrid after four successful seasons at Stamford Bridge during which he won the Club World Cup and the UEFA Conference League, as well as helping Spain triumph in the 2024 Euros. The winger made his loan move to Everton permanent this summer, departing Chelsea after progressing through our Academy and making 37 appearances for the senior team. The versatile defender spent 13 years in our Academy having joined as an Under-8. He was released at the end of the 2025/26 season, which he spent on loan at AFC Wimbledon. The Academy forward completed a permanent move to Championship side West Bromwich Albion after impressing on loan at Peterborough last season. Morgan had returned to Chelsea, where he spent time in our Academy as a youngster, in February 2023. Olise also moved on after a decade with the club. Signed by Chelsea as an Under-9, Olise featured throughout the age groups in our Academy and was named in the first-team squad for our UEFA Conference League trip to Astana during the 2024/25 season. Runham sealed a permanent switch to Ipswich Town having spent the second half of last season on loan with the Tractor Boys. The move brought the attacking midfielder's long association with Chelsea to an end. Rak-Sakyi made four first-team appearances, all in our triumphant Conference League campaign, having developed through our Academy. The midfield was released at the expiry of his contract. The midfielder made 47 appearances for Chelsea and became a full Brazil international during his three years as a Blue. He has now completed a permanent transfer to Manchester United. The Finnish youth international's six-year spell at Chelsea ended this summer. He made his first-team debut in an FA Cup win over Leeds in March 2024, and also featured in the Premier League when he came on in a home victory against Tottenham. The young defender spent the second half of last season on loan at Brentford, featuring mainly for their reserve side, and made that switch permanent over the summer.
